meta: A Christian look at the false belief that faith means never asking questions, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being told to “just believe” when you asked honest questions as a child. Leaders who treated questions as rebellion. Fear that asking will lead you away from God. A family or church where certainty was valued over understanding. Embarrassment about not knowing answers.
teaches: Scripture is full of faithful people who asked God hard questions. Habakkuk cried, “How long, O LORD?” Mary asked the angel, “How can this be?” The psalmists asked why and how long. God invited people to reason with Him. Peter tells believers to be ready to give a reason for their hope. Honest questions, brought to God with humility, can deepen faith rather than destroy it.
self_statements: Asking questions means I don’t trust God.
If I start asking, I’ll lose my faith.
God is offended by my questions.
errors: Believing you must either never question or abandon faith.
Avoiding questions because you fear where they might lead.
Overlooking the many questions asked by faithful people in Scripture.
questions: Did Habakkuk, Mary, and the psalmists ask God questions?
Did God punish them for asking?
What does Peter say I should be ready to give?
Is my faith in God, or in never having questions?
What does James 1:5 say I can ask for?
Who taught me that questions are dangerous?
What question have I been afraid to ask?
truth: Faith does not mean never asking questions. Faithful people in Scripture brought hard questions to God. I can ask honestly and humbly, seek wisdom, and trust God even when some answers do not come. My faith rests on God, not on avoiding questions.
hw_questions: Did faithful people in Scripture ask questions?
Did God punish them for asking?
What does Peter say to be ready to give?
Is my faith in God or in not asking?
What can I ask God for, according to James?
What question have I been afraid to ask?
hw_truths: I can ask God for wisdom.
My faith rests on God, not on having every answer.
I can be ready to give a reason for my hope.
log: Each day, write one honest question for God and one thing I learned while seeking.
name_example: Now if Sarah lacks wisdom, she should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to her.
actions: Write down a question you’ve been afraid to ask,
and bring it to God in prayer.
Read the whole book of Habakkuk (three short chapters),
and notice how his questions lead to trust.
Ask your pastor or a mature Christian
Look up what the Bible says about your question
using a study Bible or concordance.
tracker: One question I brought to God
prayer: Father, thank You that You welcome my honest questions. Help me reject the lie that faith means never asking questions. Give me humility, wisdom, and courage to seek You, and help me trust You even when I don’t have every answer. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Receive God’s Word with humility and allow truth to reshape thought and action.
Weariness can be expressed honestly while asking God for restoration.
Jesus is present in suffering and is greater than the circumstances we face.
What a Friend We Have in Jesus
This classic hymn invites direct, honest prayer with the Savior who carries our burdens.
